title: Close sends one journal entry per stock part on the category's account
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, whose default internal category is General Internal.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with two stock parts picked from inventory: part A, quantity 2 at a cost of $40.00, and part B, quantity 1 at a cost of $25.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • Two inventory journal entries are found, one per stock part, numbered as invoicing numbers them today.
  • Part A's entry debits account X $80.00 (2 × $40.00) and credits the inventory account the invoice would credit for that part's category and stock location.
  • Part B's entry debits account X $25.00 and credits its inventory account.
  • Nothing is debited to Cost of Parts.
  • Together they post $105.00, the Stock parts figure of the confirmation, with no invoice: no month-end reclass is needed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R2: “At Close, ShopView sends the inventory journal entries it sends at invoice today (one per picked stock part, same numbering, dated the posting date), with the debit on the expense account of the work order's category instead of the part category's cost of goods sold account or Cost of Parts, and the credit on the same inventory account the invoice would credit today (by part category and stock location). Each entry's memo carries the work order number, the classification and the category. Today these entries are sent only after the QuickBooks invoice synced; Close sends them on its own, with no invoice. The QuickBooks Class of the entry comes from the location of the work order (the mapping the location already uses for its other entries), not from a labor line's labor-rate mapping, which an internal work order does not have; without a Class on the location the entry is sent without one, as today for a part without a labor rate.”
  • Key Decisions: “Part cost goes straight to the expense account, not to cost of goods sold first, one entry per part as invoicing posts today.”
  • Goals: “For a shop on QuickBooks Online or AccountingHub, the month-end reclass journal entry for internal and no-charge jobs is no longer needed.”
  • Terminology: “Category expense account → the expense account mapped to a category per location: one ShopView Accounts row per category in QuickBooks (S5-R1), one Account Mappings row per category in AccountingHub (S6-R1). Replaces the two fixed rows Internal Work Orders Expense and Customer No-Charge Expense of v0.17.”
